items.headline: What is a *cataract?*
items.body: The most common reason people come to see us, in four slides.

items.headline: A cloudy lens
items.body: The lens inside your eye is normally clear. A cataract is that lens turning cloudy, most often with age.

items.headline: What you might notice
items.body: Blurry or dim vision, glare and halos when driving at night, colors that look faded, and glasses that need changing more often.

items.headline: It is very common
items.body: Most people develop some clouding as they get older. It is not a growth or a film on the eye, and it is not caused by using your eyes.

items.headline: And very treatable
items.body: Surgery replaces the cloudy lens with a clear one, usually one eye at a time, at an outpatient surgery center. A dilated exam tells you where you stand.
